clue.text: Chief gets quantity you'd expect

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard, as in golf's score for a hole
an amount is a quantity

explanation.surface: A boss is handed exactly the amount anyone would predict.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade runs PAR then AMOUNT, so the later phrase 'you'd expect' supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or foremost, a synonym of chief as an adjective.

clue.text: Form of transport taking one into scattered parish

indicators.note: into says the letter for one goes inside the rearranged parish letters
scattered tells us the letters of parish are strewn about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying a single passenger around a spread-out rural parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges PARISH, and 'taking one into' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible balloon is a flying vehicle, so it is a kind of transport.

clue.text: A Mediterranean island said to grow with extra bits being added

definitions.text: grow with extra bits being added

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: A plus Crete, the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: An island in the Med is reputed to expand as more pieces get added on.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a Crete' sounds just like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to build up gradually by layers or particles sticking on, a technical verb for growth by accumulation.

clue.text: River going north and south — place showing reverse

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the river's name is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
the same river again, this time going south, so read downwards and forwards
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A river flowing both ways, and a spot showing the other side of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' does double duty as the same river flowing both ways: 'going north' reverses it in this down entry, and 'south' leaves the second copy reading downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of something is its contrary, which is what the noun reverse means.

clue.text: Couple hand over money, we hear, for personal cover

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: a couple is two; to pay is to hand over money

explanation.surface: A pair settle a bill for something to cover themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: TWO PAY, said aloud, sounds like the hairpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig covering a bald patch is a cover for one's own head, hence a personal cover.

clue.text: Three magi bowled over in a secluded place

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked flat, so the letters of three magi are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The Three Wise Men are astonished in some remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' looks like amazement at the Nativity, but it rearranges THREE MAGI.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit's dwelling is a retreat away from people, so a secluded place.

clue.text: Journalist and French soldier in carriage

parts.note: hack is slang for a journalist
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A reporter and a French trooper ride in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: A hackney carriage is a horse-drawn cab for hire; London taxis are still licensed under that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is a hired horse-drawn coach, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Wandered right into performance, following plan

indicators.note: following says the plan word comes before the rest

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it

indicators.note: into puts the letter for right inside the word for performance

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance

explanation.surface: Someone strayed into a show as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' builds DERED from performance and right, and 'following' puts that after the plan word.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to take a winding, aimless course, which is how one wanders.

clue.text: Old lady with couple of teeth at the front stuffed herself?

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

indicators.note: couple of means two letters are wanted from the word teeth
at the front says those two letters are its opening ones

explanation.surface: A grandmother with only her front teeth left still managed to gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' suggests MA or a mother, but it splits into O and VERA. The question mark flags that the definition is just one instance of overeating.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to eat too much, which is what someone who stuffed herself did.

clue.text: Canon's very quiet time going round about church

indicators.note: going round says the quiet and time letters encircle the next pieces

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
re is Latin for about, as in business letters
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cathedral cleric's hush-hush moment spent circling the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a clergyman, but it is the rule. The 's stands for 'is'. RECE goes inside PP T, after the first P.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general rule or principle, as is a precept.

clue.text: Ask relations for fruit

parts.note: to pump someone is to ask them questions persistently
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Asking the family to pass the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A large orange gourd counts botanically as a fruit.

clue.text: In book here's wicked little group

indicators.note: In says the scrambled letters go inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a book, especially a large one

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of here's taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a novel lies a bit of villainy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges the letters of here's into HREES, and 'In' sets them inside the book.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is three people together, a small group.

clue.text: Fellow taking time to establish authority

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a date is a time

explanation.surface: A man takes his time to assert who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An electoral mandate is the authority given to act, as a winning party claims.

clue.text: Tease the silly person trying to be arty

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are messed about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Mock that ridiculous would-be bohemian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' seems to describe the person, but it rearranges TEASE THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who poses as a lover of art and beauty fits a person straining to seem cultured.

clue.text: Most clever chap tested — only 6/10!

indicators.note: only six of the ten letters of chap tested are taken, the six inside it

explanation.surface: A lad who was examined and scored a lowly sixty percent is called the cleverest.
explanation.walkthrough: '6/10' looks like a poor mark, but it says six of the ten letters of 'chap tested' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt can mean quick to learn, so the superlative means cleverest.

clue.text: Earlier idea so far out

indicators.note: out means wrong or off the mark, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A previous notion so far proved wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IDEA SO FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid means mentioned before, so earlier in a text.

clue.text: Securing a poor building built on heather

indicators.note: built on says, in this down clue, the building sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: a shack is a crude, poorly made hut
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Putting up a ramshackle hut on the moor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, SHACK is placed above LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackling means fastening with chains, a way of securing someone.

clue.text: The man, a big noise, given grand title

parts.note: he refers to a man
a din is a loud noise
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A loud VIP is given a fine name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' sounds like an important person, but it is DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A heading is the caption at the top of a page or section, its title.

clue.text: What is more restricted and possibly rarer now

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement of the letters of rarer now

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something tighter, and perhaps less common these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RARER NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrower means of smaller width, so more limited or confined.

clue.text: Monetary support very good, south African party admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the party goes inside the word for very good

parts.note: fine means very good
the ANC, the African National Congress, is South Africa's main party

explanation.surface: A grand cash backing lets in a South African political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'south African party' as 'South African party'; 'admitted' lets it into the word for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Funding is money provided to back a project, the support meant here.

clue.text: A woman taking drug in epic tale

indicators.note: taking means the woman's name takes the drug inside it

parts.note: Enid is a woman's name
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman taking narcotics features in an old saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts E inside ENID, after the opening A. The answer is Virgil's Latin poem about Aeneas.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's poem of Aeneas's wanderings is an epic, a long heroic narrative.

clue.text: Fantastic man, 'lion' so-called

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful, so the letters of man and lion are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An imaginary man said to be a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges MAN and LION together.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means in name only, existing merely as described, like so-called.

clue.text: Like some rock genius, troubled about nothing

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the letter for nothing
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of genius are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind, worried about having nothing, is rock-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges GENIUS, and 'about' wraps those letters round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rocks form from cooled magma, so the adjective describes one class of rock.

clue.text: Artist gets in bed having grabbed a garment

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

indicators.note: having grabbed says the bed word holds the letter A inside it

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A painter climbs into bed after snatching some clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' tempts as a container, but IN is a piece; 'having grabbed' is the container, the bed holding A.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof coat is a garment worn in wet weather.

clue.text: A theologian? The little fellow becomes rotten

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
Les is the short form of the man's name Leslie, a little name for a fellow

explanation.surface: Is a religious scholar's young son going bad?
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals a shortened name: LES for Leslie.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg that addles goes bad, so the verb means turns rotten.

clue.text: Damage put right in time — dent on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the letters of dent surround the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the letter for right is placed inside the word time

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fixing a fault promptly, apart from a dent on the bodywork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' looks like repair, but it means put R: 'in' makes TRIME, and 'on the outside' wraps dent around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or loss suffered, which is damage.

clue.text: Unhappy about walk that may be printed in newspaper

definitions.text: that may be printed in newspaper

indicators.note: about means around, so the unhappy word goes round the walk

parts.note: sad means unhappy
a mall is a shaded public walk, as with The Mall in London

explanation.surface: A gloomy account of a stroll appears in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A mall was first a tree-lined public promenade, as with The Mall in London; 'about' puts it inside the unhappy word.
explanation.definitionFit: A classified advertisement is a short notice published in a newspaper.

clue.text: Actress's final performance no good

definitions.note: the 's is read as 'is', so the definition is just the actress

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a swan song is a last performance before retiring

explanation.surface: A star's farewell show was a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson was the star of Sunset Boulevard. 'no good' removes G from SWAN SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood film star of the silent and early sound era.

clue.text: In church primarily that's seen swirling?

definitions.text: In church primarily that's seen swirling?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of church is used
swirling means whirling about, so the letters of seen are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something seen drifting about inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, then C, the first letter of 'church', then ENSE, from 'swirling' SEEN. As a whole the clue describes the fragrant smoke drifting in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Burned aromatic resin gives smoke that drifts and curls around a church during services.

clue.text: Lis, it would appear, makes the final cut

explanation.surface: Someone named Lis is picked for the last round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lis' is a list missing its last letter, so it looks like a list cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Lis is a list with its end lopped off; and a list of finalists after selection is the final cut.
